title: DACH private beta launch cheat sheet
content:
Purpose
This is a compact internal cheat sheet for the DACH private beta of Redwood Private (region-limited offering + enhanced compliance). Intended audience: GTM reps, solutions engineers, partner managers, and launch PMs. Not customer-facing.

High-level launch thesis
We are launching a DACH private-beta focused on regulated mid-market and enterprise buyers who require strict data residency, KMS integration, and a local deployment footprint. Messaging should emphasize predictable inference economics, enterprise controls, and a friction-minimized onboarding path for platform and security teams.

Priority buyer personas
- Platform/ML Infra leads: care about performance, deterministic latency, throughput, and autoscaling in private environments.
- Security & Compliance leads: care about KMS/HSM, audit logs, SOC2/ISO equivalence, and contractual data residency.
- Product/AI engineering managers: want easy SDKs, model rollouts, and ability to fallback to hosted variants during peak.
- Procurement/Legal: need clear SLAs and contract guardrails.

Key one-line positioning (EN)
Redwood Private DACH beta: enterprise-grade LLM inference with local data residency, predictable performance, and unified tooling across hosted and private deployments.

German-friendly headline (short)
Redwood Private (DACH beta): Lokale Datenhaltung, SLA‑Performance, einfache Onboarding‑Pfad

Three core messages (lead with what matters)
1) Production economics, not research demos: predictable token costs, batch/cache controls, and SKU-based reserved capacity for budgeting.
2) Compliance-first private deployment: region-restricted control plane, KMS integrations, and audit trails for regulated workloads.
3) Same developer experience across environments: identical API/SDK, rollout controls, and built-in fallbacks to hosted models for burst capacity.

Proof points / evidence to surface (short)
- Benchmarks: 99th percentile latency targets for common LLM families (attach per-model bench doc).
- SLA: 99.95% uptime for dedicated pools; detailed SLOs in legal appendix.
- Integrations: KMS (AWS KMS + Azure Key Vault), Okta SSO example, and on-prem network topology options.
- Customer pilot: early pilot with FinanzSolutions GmbH (anonymized) showed 35% cost reduction vs self-hosted baseline under similar throughput.

Competitive callouts & how to position against them
- AWS Bedrock / SageMaker endpoints: emphasize that Redwood offers a unified developer experience across hosted and private with explicit cost-levers and rollout tooling. Bedrock is broad but not tuned for predictable per-token economics or opinionated fallback policies.
- OpenAI: strong model capability but limited private deployment options and control over data residency. Lead with privacy and KMS story.
- Anthropic / Cohere: good models; position Redwood as the inference platform that operationalizes models with cost and reliability controls.
- Self-hosted inference stacks (internal infra, runbooks): we remove heavy ops by providing optimized runtime, autoscaling, and observability out of box.

Objection handling snippets
- "We can just host our own": You can, but the engineering and ops burden is significant. Redwood provides a GPU-optimized runtime with autoscaling, kernel selection and KV cache strategies tuned for production LLM usage that reduces TCO and time-to-market.
- "How about data residency/legal?": The DACH private beta enforces regional control plane placement, offers customer-managed keys, and captures audit logs. Legal will provide region-specific contract language during pilot.
- "How do you compare on latency?": We provide per-route latency SLOs and deterministic batching settings. Share model-specific 50/95/99 latency tables from infra bench doc.

Internal enablement checklist (what GTM needs before first outreach)
- Sales kits: localized one-pager (DE/EN), competitor battle cards (DE), pricing guidance for reserved capacity.
- Demos: recorded demo showing KMS integration and canary rollout in DACH region.
- SRE/SE readiness: runbook for customer onboarding, region provisioning checklist, and escalation matrix.
- Legal & procurement: approved pilot contract template with DACH-specific data residency clauses.
- Support: 24/5 pilot support rotation and named SE for first three pilots.
- Marketing assets: localized landing page, press FAQ, 2 partner enablement webinars scheduled in CET hours.

Announcement draft (internal / partner) — short English
Subject: Redwood Private DACH beta — regional private deployment for regulated workloads
Body: We are kicking off a DACH private beta focused on regulated enterprise customers. The beta includes region-restricted control plane, KMS integrations, and reserved capacity options. Reach out to the GTM leads to nominate pilot customers. Please use the pilot qualification spreadsheet linked in the GTM JIRA.

Announcement draft (customer-facing, German) — short
Betreff: Einladung zur Redwood Private DACH Beta
Text: Wir laden ausgewählte Unternehmen zur Teilnahme an unserer Redwood Private DACH Beta ein. Die Beta bietet lokale Datenhaltung, Schlüsselverwaltung über Ihren KMS und garantierte Performance‑SLOs. Bei Interesse melden Sie sich bei Ihrem Account Manager. Weitere Details auf Anfrage.

Rep / SE email template for outbound (short)
Hi <Name>,
We are opening a limited DACH private beta for teams with strict data residency and compliance needs. Redwood provides a turnkey private deployment with KMS integration, audit logs, and predictable inference costs. Would you be interested in a 30–45 minute pilot scoping session next week?

Localization notes
- Translate collateral into German; prioritize legal/contract summaries and customer-facing one-pager.
- Use CET times for webinars and demo sessions; avoid CET/CEST ambiguity in scheduling.
- Localize examples and case studies to DACH-regional names where possible.

Operational asks for engineering (beta readiness)
- Region availability: ensure DACH region images are available and documented (ticket infra#456).
- KMS: validate AWS KMS and Azure Key Vault flows end-to-end with a test tenant.
- Telemetry: enable enhanced audit logs + per-token cost attribution for pilot tenants.
- Rollout policies: test canary and automatic fallback to hosted variants on simulated capacity loss.

Metrics to track during beta
- Time to first inference (minutes) for pilot onboarding.
- 95/99 latency percentiles on representative workloads.
- Billing variance: expected vs actual token cost per pilot.
- Support SLA breaches and mean time to resolve (MTTR).

Risks and open questions
- Legal: need sign-off on DACH contract language before public customer outreach. (Owner: Legal, ticket CON-1234).
- Capacity: confirm reserved pool sizing for first three pilots to avoid noisy neighbor risk.
- Pricing: final guidance on reserved capacity discounts vs hosted tiers still pending finance approval.

Next steps and timeline (high level)
- Week 0: finalize pilot contract and sales kit (legal + GTM).
- Week 1–2: onboard first two pilot customers; run integration checklist.
- Week 3–6: iterate on telemetry, collect soff feedback, capture cost/latency metrics.
- Week 8: review pilot outcomes and decide on wider roll out.

Notes to self / loose items
- Coordinate demo recording with Arjun and Clara; include German subtitles.
- Confirm GCP region parity request: ask infra whether GCP DACH expansion is feasible.
- Draft press FAQ but mark as internal until legal approves statements on SLAs.

References and quick links
- Pilot qualification sheet: JIRA:GTM-427
- Infra PR for region images: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/456
- Contracts draft: https://confluence.redwood.company/pages/CON-1234

Do not publish without legal sign-off. This is a working cheat sheet — expect edits as pilots progress.
